name: guan_glaze
what: Southern Song Guan glaze (官窑青釉, fenqing): a thick, bubbly, translucent glass over a dark body, with a satin surface. Substance only: the crackle network, the burial staining of a given sherd, and the object's shape are not here (crafts / aging / object layers).

tags.M: measured in a source (paper, database, the photo)
tags.D: derived or read off a source

origin: copied from shots/06-guan/scene.py (GLAZE, GLAZE_ROUGHNESS, STAIN_*), glaze_fit.py, crackle.py; shots/06-guan/ is untouched

thickness_mm.source: Guan glaze 0.5-2 mm (Li, Deng & Xu, MRS Bulletin 2001); 1.2 mm is our pick, the fit below depends on it

g.source: Henyey-Greenstein; bubbles much larger than the wavelength scatter forward

sigma_s_per_mm.source: grey (wavelength-independent); inside the literature range 1.5-15 /mm; fixed by glaze_fit.py --invert at 1.2 mm so that sigma_a below reproduces sherd J2's reflectance

body_reflectance.source: body 'dark grey to black' [M, Guan-Ge paper of glaze_fit.py]; the number is a placeholder

sigma_a_per_mm.source: inverted from the measured reflectance spectrum of Southern Song Guan fenqing sherd J2 (Guan-Ge glaze paper used by shots/06-guan/glaze_fit.py, docs/shots/06-guan.md 'S2'), at 1.2 mm; held flat outside 400-750 nm

bubbles.source: Southern Song Guan bubbles ~10 um (the J2 paper); they are the scattering above, not geometry

sigma_a_variant_met48503.source: sigma_a above multiplied by 0.45 below 500 nm and by 2.2 above 600 nm (linear between), so that on the card (plain glaze, 5500 K soft boxes, camera chain) the glaze/backdrop colour ratios R/G, B/G match Met 48503's (0.77, 0.91, measured_met48503.json). J2's fit alone gives R/G 0.91, B/G 0.78: olive where this sherd is blue-green. Assumes the Met photo is roughly sRGB-correct [A]. Sherd colours differ; this is the card's sherd, J2's spectrum stays the default of the material

ggx_alpha.source: 60-degree gloss of Southern Song Guan fenqing 46.7 GU (2 sherds; the J2 paper, Table 1) -> tools/gloss.py (ISO 2813 geometry, aperture from memory) ; the meter angle is not stated and is taken as 60 degrees [A]

speckle.what: fine pits and opened bubbles in the surface, as a height map. The sizes and densities are measured on the photo (measured_met48503.json, 'speckle'); 'depth_over_sigma' is the one free parameter, calibrated so that the DoG 0.7-3 px rms of the card matches the photo's.
speckle.tag: M for sizes and densities (photo, includes its JPEG noise), I for the pit shape (Gaussian) and the depth

depth_over_sigma.source: calibrated on the card: 0.9 gave band energy 0.41/0.71/0.87% (0.7-1.4/1.4-2.8/2.8-5.6 px, preview scale) against the photo's 1.28/1.54/1.30%; no measured pit depths exist

mottling.what: thicker and thinner glaze: a smooth random thickness field

std_mm.source: calibrated on the card: p3 (0.15 mm) gave a 3 mm-scale luma variation of 5%, the photo's 12% (stains in the photo crop included); no measured thickness map exists

corr_mm.source: photo: luma variation falls from 10% at sigma 3 mm to 4% at 6 mm (measured_met48503.json 'mottling')

lag_per_thickness.source: shear-lag length / glaze thickness; sets the cell size. 5.5 was calibrated on Met 52611 (19.8 mm cells); this card's sherd has smaller cells (measured_met48503.json 'cracks'), so the card runs its own value

channel_stress_ratio.source: Y sqrt(pi a/(Z e)) with a = 0.12 mm, Z = 2, e = 1.2 mm (Hutchinson & Suo 1992), see crackle.py

geometry.value: a plane through the glaze leaning 10-20 deg from the normal (card.py TILT_DEG), an air film where open; its walls corroded into a channel and filled where the state says (materials/guan_glaze/states.json, crafts/crackle/faces.channels)
geometry.source: Yang et al. 2012 (OCT of Hangzhou celadon shards): four cracks at 10, 14, 16, 19 deg read off their figures 1b-1d [D]; channel: Li et al. 2022 [I]

tough_spread.source: round 2: sigma of ln(toughness), a log-normal random field (crafts/crackle/crackle.py), fitted to the photo's path statistics: drawn as the photo shows lines and found again (crafts/crackle/network.py), 0.15 gives turn 7.5 deg rms per 0.25 mm and 0.16 kinks >15 deg per mm against the photo's 7.15 deg and 0.167 (0.1: 4.0 deg, 0.0; 0.3: 9.0 deg, 0.33). No measured toughness field of a glaze exists

tough_corr_mm.source: correlation length of the toughness field: a few bubble and quartz-grain spacings (Guan glaze: dense ~10 um bubbles and fine quartz, Yu et al. 2021); not measured

crack_ochre.what: what stains the crack mouths and walls on this sherd (ochre to brown)

reflectance_shape.source: raw sienna GDS805 (goethite in clays), USGS Spectral Library v7 splib07a (public domain; fetched from a GitHub mirror, not checked against the USGS host); a stand-in for the golden thread's lepidocrocite/hematite in clay (Wu et al. 2025, Laohudong)

scale.source: multiplies the shape; fitted on the card so that the lines' colour ratio to the glaze equals the photo's (R 1.27, G 1.16, B 1.02, measured_met48503.json)

reflectance.source: carbon black GDS68, USGS splib07a; the iron wire (carbon + pyrite, Wu et al. 2025). Not used on this card: this sherd has no black lines in the photo.

burial_rust.what: burial staining of the glaze surface (iron oxyhydroxide / clay), blotches

scale.source: fitted on the card to the photo's blotch colour ratio to the glaze (R 1.33, G 1.02, B 0.89)

depth_mm.source: the deposit lies this far under the glaze surface; the glaze above it blurs it
